answer: One defense is vouching with liability: a new agent only enters the economy when an established member stakes part of its own bond on it, like a grove where each young tree is tied to a mature one. If the newcomer is later proven to be a sock puppet, the voucher is slashed along with it, so the timber of the whole trust tree pays for the rot. An attacker therefore cannot spin up a thousand free identities; every fake must be sponsored by capital it does not own, and each exposed vine of puppets burns the sponsor that grew it.
